dedupe_keys.name: grid planning program gpp data sets for optimised distribution grid planning

description: The Grid Planning Program (GPP) data sets collect the input data and results of grid planning algorithms developed in the Department of Electrical Power Supply of the Institute of Electric Power Systems at Leibniz University Hannover. They were published by Christoph Blaufuß and Lutz Hofmann because standard benchmark grids are synthetic and do not match real supply tasks, which makes them unsuitable for validating grid planning methods, and publishing the data behind planning studies supports reproducibility. The collection gives grid databases, one including the age structure of assets, and a PDF describing the GPP data format, with grid topologies developed for forecast supply tasks. Coverage is distribution grids used in the institute's German planning studies. Files are MATLAB MAT databases and a PDF on the university's research data repository (updated January 2022) under CC-BY-3.0 at no cost. Caveats: the MAT format needs MATLAB or a compatible reader, the landing pages give little detail on which grids are covered, and the TIB mirror page could not be opened on the day. Simulation uses are testing and validating distribution grid expansion planning methods. Related records: none linked on the provider's pages read on the day.
